title: Transforming Schema
strapline: Water into mud, dry into wet, juice into the sand — the child gripped by changing one thing into another.
intent: Recognise transforming as a schema — the fascination with changing materials: mixing, melting, adding water, watching one thing become another.
Understand the learning inside it: cause and effect, states and properties, reversible and irreversible change.
Read the deliberate mixing of everything into everything as experiment, not spoiling — the change is the whole point.
Build sensory and scientific curiosity through pouring, stirring, mixing and combining.
Feed the language of change — melting, mixing, dissolving, going hard, turning brown — spoken as it happens.
implementation: Offer materials that change: water and soil for mud, cornflour gloop, ice to melt, dough, sand and water, colour to mix.
Provide tools for combining — jugs, spoons, whisks, pipettes, pots — and let the mixing run.
Name the transformation as it happens ('you added water and the flour turned to sticky paste!').
Value the mud-kitchen mess for what it is: a laboratory where dry becomes wet and separate becomes mixed.
Set up reversible changes (ice melting, water freezing) and simple safe mixes, and let children lead the combining.
key_questions: What happened when you mixed them together?
Is it getting wetter or drier?
Where has the ice gone — what did it turn into?
What will happen if we add more water?
How did you make the colour change?

impact.text: A child mixes and combines materials to change them, discovering that adding one thing to another makes something new.
Toddlers pour, stir, whisk and mix with enthusiasm and their own agenda, hands deep in changing materials.
Children explore change with every sense — mud, gloop, melting ice, colour swirling into water.
The language of change surfaces as toddlers name what they see — 'wet', 'gone', 'more', 'all mixed'.

enhancements: A mud kitchen with soil, water and real pots for turning dry into wet.
Cornflour gloop that flows and sets under the hands.
Ice to melt, and water to freeze overnight and find changed.
Colour-mixing with pipettes, water and a few drops of paint.
Baking-style play — flour, water and dough that changes as it is worked.

playing_exploring: The child combines materials freely, chasing the moment one thing becomes another.
Change is explored with hands, tools and all the senses.
active_learning: Toddlers mix and remix, repeating the change and adjusting to make it happen again.
creating_thinking: Children predict and test — what if I add water, what if I mix these? — and watch to see what changes.
